title: A Day in Kyoto
summaryZh: 作者回憶在京都的一整天，從清晨的寺廟一路騎車到夜晚的河邊。

sentences.text: I woke up before sunrise on my second morning in Kyoto.
sentences.zh: 在京都的第二天早上，我在日出前就醒了。
sentences.note: woke up 連讀成 /woʊkʌp/；before 的第一個音節弱讀成 /bɪ/。

sentences.text: The streets were empty, and the air felt cool and clean.
sentences.zh: 街道空無一人，空氣又涼又乾淨。

sentences.text: I walked twenty minutes to a small temple near the hills.
sentences.zh: 我走了二十分鐘，到山邊的一間小寺廟。
sentences.note: twenty 口語常唸成 /ˈtwɛni/，中間的 t 幾乎消失。

sentences.text: Only a few people were there, so it stayed very quiet.
sentences.zh: 那裡只有幾個人，所以一直都很安靜。

sentences.text: I sat on the wooden steps and watched the light change.
sentences.zh: 我坐在木頭階梯上，看著光線慢慢改變。

sentences.text: Later, I bought a rice ball and green tea from a shop.
sentences.zh: 後來我在一家小店買了飯糰和綠茶。
sentences.note: Later 的 t 是閃音 /ˈleɪɾɚ/；bought a 連讀成 /bɔɾə/。

sentences.text: The woman behind the counter smiled and taught me two words.
sentences.zh: 櫃台後的女士對我微笑，還教了我兩個單字。

sentences.text: In the afternoon, I rented a bike and rode along the river.
sentences.zh: 下午我租了一台腳踏車，沿著河邊騎。
sentences.note: rented a → /ˈrɛnɪɾə/，第一個 t 常省略，第二個變閃音。

sentences.text: The path was flat, so I rode for almost two hours.
sentences.zh: 那條路很平，所以我騎了將近兩個小時。

sentences.text: I passed old wooden houses with tiny gardens by the water.
sentences.zh: 我經過一棟棟老木屋，河邊還有小小的庭院。

sentences.text: By evening, my legs were tired, but I didn't care at all.
sentences.zh: 到了傍晚，我的腿很酸，但我一點也不在意。
sentences.note: didn't 的 t 在句中常不爆破，聽起來像 /ˈdɪdn̩/。

sentences.text: I found a small place that served noodles and cold beer.
sentences.zh: 我找到一家小店，賣麵和冰啤酒。

sentences.text: After dinner, I walked back along the river in the dark.
sentences.zh: 吃完晚餐，我在黑夜裡沿著河邊走回去。

sentences.text: People sat on the bank, talking and laughing in small groups.
sentences.zh: 有人三三兩兩坐在河岸上聊天、大笑。

sentences.text: It was a simple day, and I'll remember it for years.
sentences.zh: 那是很簡單的一天，但我會記得好多年。
sentences.note: I'll 在快速口語中幾乎只剩 /aɪl/，別漏聽這個未來式。

questions.q: Why were the streets quiet when the writer went out?
How did the writer travel in the afternoon?
How did the writer feel at the end of the day?
